beats.trigger: ## Getting Going
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: With the right guardrails, you create output that's genuinely yours, not generic.
beats.got: Claim that AI output can be made personal. Plausible, unproven.

beats.trigger: Build a snake game as HTML.
beats.got: Homework I did not do. A snake game is a toy.

beats.trigger: **Package** the guardrails as reusable rules
beats.got: Four verbs. Bloom's taxonomy again. Nothing new.

beats.trigger: where did LLM output on your own work come out generic, and what made it feel like yours?
beats.got: A fair question, at least one I can answer from my own use.

beats.trigger: The same question. Two answers. What makes the difference?
beats.got: A teaser slide. Fine.

beats.trigger: The first exchange became context.
beats.got: An earlier unrelated question steers the later answer. I can try this in five minutes myself.

beats.trigger: The LLM reads the whole conversation every time and generates the next response from all of it.
beats.got: Plain mechanism, no hype. This is how it works.

beats.trigger: You told the LLM who you are.
beats.got: Telling it a role changes the answer. I half knew this from chat already.

beats.trigger: Tools, goals, checks, boundaries, and loops come later and depend on it.
beats.got: A list of future vocabulary. Framework-sounding.

beats.trigger: You write it once, and it shapes every answer.
beats.got: A persistent instruction file the agent loads each session. That is different from my chat use. 'That's your turn' is a bit cute.

beats.trigger: Change the context, watch the agent's output shift, then package what you learned for the next session.
beats.got: 45 minutes on a personal website. For a telecom director.

beats.trigger: It works, but it's generic.
beats.got: Paste my LinkedIn, get a generic page. Expected, but I get to see the baseline myself.

beats.trigger: not *"I should book a discovery call."*
beats.got: The site should not sell. Fine.

beats.trigger: The LLM already knows StoryBrand, so you don't reproduce the questions.
beats.got: I can name a framework I know and the model applies it. Useful, I know SWOT and Kata.

beats.trigger: StoryBrand shapes only the colleague-help section.
beats.got: Fiddly instruction about who is the hero of the page.

beats.trigger: List 3-5 strengths, one line each.
beats.got: Self-description homework. Feels like an HR workshop.

beats.trigger: Most people can list what drives them mad at work in thirty seconds, but stall for five minutes on what they're great at.
beats.got: True. I could list my hates faster than my strengths. Annoyingly accurate.

beats.trigger: "decks where every page says 'iterating'"
beats.got: Vague input gives the default me. Specific hates give something sharper. That I can write.

beats.trigger: The agent is reading its own work where it wrote it, and LLMs go easy on their own output.
beats.got: They admit the tool flatters itself and tell me how to work around it. Candid.

beats.trigger: *"Make it look like Stripe's design language"*
beats.got: Restyling by naming a site. Cute, not my job.

beats.trigger: The chat summary rounds corners; the file is what travels
beats.got: The output of the session is a rules file I can reuse, and I should read it myself and not trust the summary.

beats.trigger: The more specific the context, the more the output is yours.
beats.got: Specific input gives specific output. Not surprising, but properly demonstrated.

beats.trigger: The same mechanism scales to business proposals, competitor analysis, compliance reviews and product strategy
beats.got: A big claim with no evidence, which is what I distrust. 'Recipe 1' sounds like a franchise.

beats.trigger: ## Iterate and Learn
beats.got: nothing new

beats.trigger: The move: change something, notice what shifted, adjust, build again.
beats.got: Iteration loop, plain PDCA. Seen it.

beats.trigger: Agreeable answers won the round the model was tuned on.
beats.got: The model is trained to be agreeable, so it grades its own work kindly. A real limitation, said plainly.

beats.trigger: Where it doesn't, yours counts.
beats.got: Treat the agent's report as a claim and check it against what I saw. That is ordinary management.

beats.trigger: Only you could catch a wrong line about you, which is why your own profile is the place to start.
beats.got: The test is my own knowledge. Sensible, and a reason the exercise used my own profile.

beats.trigger: Nobody knows where agents are going, not Anthropic, not your board.
beats.got: Honest about uncertainty, which I respect. 'Felt experience' is a bit much, but the McKinsey line is fair.

beats.trigger: Expect the generation rules to change a lot. The first pass is rarely right.
beats.got: The rules file gets a second pass by the agent. Admitting the first draft is poor is good.

beats.trigger: **compound interest on a rule file.**
beats.got: Keep correcting the file. 'Compound interest' is slogan territory.

beats.trigger: Your gut on what is uniquely you carries more weight than the agent's.
beats.got: A second, independent reviewer with no context, and my judgement stays the arbiter. I can test that.

beats.trigger: Guardrails are structured context, not a checklist.
beats.got: Summary of what I already took in.

beats.trigger: Bring a live challenge and working access to Confluence and OneDrive.
beats.got: More homework, and access that may need IT approval.

beats.trigger: Karpathy's LLM Wiki post; Lindenberg's memory-architecture piece, optional.
beats.got: Reading list.

beats.trigger: leave yourself a three-line readiness note.
beats.got: Admin before the next session.

beats.trigger: If stuck, scan your next two weeks of calendar; the biggest unresolved item is usually your challenge.
beats.got: Pick a real open problem. I have plenty.

beats.trigger: If a connector needs admin approval, tell the training coordinator and keep going.
beats.got: Connecting the agent to company wikis and drives. Legal will ask about that first.

beats.trigger: Before it writes anything, ask it for a plan and approve or revise it first.
beats.got: Make it show a plan before it edits files. Sensible control.

beats.trigger: If a line is blank, name a fallback; do not fill it with a plausible answer.
beats.got: Write a three-line note. The warning against plausible filler is a good one.

beats.trigger: a useful system is a living pile of text the agent can read, maintain, and improve.
beats.got: Another reading assignment.

beats.trigger: The output now travels with a file the agent re-reads next time.
beats.got: Next module builds on the file idea.

take_homes: What I put in first steers what comes out. A persistent file of instructions is something I haven't used in chat.
The model flatters its own work, so I check its report against what I know and get a cold second reader.
Specific input, like real things I hate, beats general descriptions of me.

monday.move: Nothing on Monday as a programme. At most, try the dinner test and a persistent instructions file on one real task, such as a partner brief, and see whether the output differs.
monday.stop_condition: If the output is not clearly better than my plain chat prompt after two tries, I drop it.
monday.blocker: Steering groups for the last programme, and the Module 2 prework I have not done.

misconception.why: They told me the tool's weaknesses plainly, and the persistent file is a real difference from chat. But a personal website exercise does not show me a business difference, so I'm still waiting to see it on real work. Wait-and-see is less comfortable than before, not gone.

one_line: Less hype than I expected and it was honest about where the thing fools you, but I did a personal website, so ask me again when it has done something for the business.
